intro.title: Browser compatibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web application that checks if a user's browser supports a modern JavaScript feature, such as the `fetch` API. You will learn the core concept of browser compatibility, which involves detecting browser capabilities to ensure your code works across different environments. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's feature detection, conditional logic, and the Document Object Model (DOM) for displaying results. By the end, you'll understand how to write code that adapts to various browsers, making your web apps more reliable and accessible.
intro.usecase: Browser compatibility is essential when building web applications that must work consistently across different user environments. Developers encounter this daily when implementing features like interactive dashboards that need to render charts correctly in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari, or forms with modern CSS Grid layouts that must degrade gracefully in older browsers. E-commerce checkout flows, banking interfaces, and collaborative tools like Figma or Google Docs all require careful compatibility testing to ensure every user has a seamless experience regardless of their browser choice.
